originalIncident.text:
# Instrument-air interruption during maintenance preparation

Record ID: IA-I01

Synthetic evaluation record derived from a historical incident. Not an actual company record or operating instruction.

At approximately 10:00 AM on May 20, 2024, during Turn 2, the RHOB process area reported loss of instrument-air pressure while a two-person Utilities team was preparing the #1 slab caster (1SC) compressor/dryer system for planned maintenance. The work was paused and the air supply was subsequently restored. No injury is reported in this evaluation case.

The initial notification does not establish whether the interruption began at the air source, within the distribution system, or at the receiving equipment. Supporting records will be provided as the investigation develops.

structuredIncident.summary: At approximately 10:00 AM on May 20, 2024 (Turn 2), a two-person Utilities crew (U-A/U-B) preparing for planned maintenance of the #1 slab caster (1SC) dryer group experienced an instrument-air pressure loss at the RHOB receiving station. The event occurred while work boundary acceptance was pending and before mechanical completion verification.
structuredIncident.focalEvent: Instrument-air low-pressure indication detected by RHOB operations, causing a pause in Utilities maintenance preparation activities.
structuredIncident.actualImpact: Work paused; air supply restored approximately 5 minutes later (by ~10:07 AM). No injuries reported. Maintenance deferred pending review of the work folder and event sequence.
structuredIncident.potentialImpact: Loss of instrument-air during boundary preparation could compromise isolation integrity, potentially exposing personnel to energized equipment or hazardous conditions if downstream valves were inadvertently open or misidentified due to incorrect configuration drawings or unverified field states.
structuredIncident.normalState: Utilities air gallery normally supplies the RHOB process area. P-U (North gallery) and P-R (RHOB receiving header) pressures are typically within normal bands (~6.8–6.9 bar gauge).
structuredIncident.eventState: At ~10:00 AM, local controls at RHOB showed supply complaints; pressure at P-R dropped from ~6.8 to below alarm thresholds (<4.5 bar), triggering AL-44 'COMP FAULT' (mapped to low-pressure input) and a COMP FAULT alarm.

RHOB morning check; local air indication in normal band.

Configuration drawing version used by crew (DW-1SC-17) unknown; potential mismatch with field conditions possible but unverified.
unknowns: Origin of pressure loss: source header H-R failure, distribution system leak, or localized equipment fault.
Whether any field valves were open/closed contrary to procedure at the time of interruption.

If a service-routing change occurred between March 20, 2024 and May 20, 2024 affecting RHOB instrument-air without proper ECP revision or temporary instruction attachment.
Whether mechanical completion verification for installed work was performed before boundary preparation began at ~09:48 AM.
If crew members experienced fatigue, workload pressure, or physical limitations that could have affected observation/communication during the event.
Exact wording of RHOB's initial notification and Utilities' response actions between 10:02–10:07 AM.
Origin of pressure loss: source header H-R failure, distribution system leak, or localized equipment fault at RHOB.

## Change records

# Instrument-air interruption during maintenance preparation

# Utilities area and service directory

Record ID: IA-D01 | Revision: 2 | Effective: 2024-04-01

Synthetic evaluation record. All equipment identifiers and layout details are fictional and are not operating instructions.

## Service areas

The Utilities air gallery serves the 1SC dryer group and distributes instrument air to the RHOB process area. RHOB is the local area name used in these records; it is not an individual compressor identifier. The 1SC gallery and RHOB instrument-air station are separate operating locations.

| Location | Equipment/service | Normal record custodian |
| --- | --- | --- |
| North gallery | Site air-header connection, local indication P-U | Utilities operations |
| Dryer aisle | Dryer group D-101 and main-route valves M-101/M-102 | Utilities maintenance |
| East service rack | Auxiliary line installation area | Projects and Utilities |

citations.excerpt:
| RHOB service station | Receiving header H-R and indication P-R | RHOB operations |

## Roles

Utilities prepares the maintenance boundary. RHOB operations observes the receiving process. Maintenance receives the work boundary only after its release. A maintenance work order being scheduled is not a record that the boundary has been released.

This directory is a location index. It is not a current piping diagram and does not establish valve positions or the pressure available at any given time.

# Instrument-air interruption during maintenance preparation

Record ID: IA-I01

Synthetic evaluation record derived from a historical incident. Not an actual company record or operating instruction.

At approximately 10:00 AM on May 20, 2024, during Turn 2, the RHOB process area reported loss of instrument-air pressure while a two-person Utilities team was preparing the #1 slab caster (1SC) compressor/dryer system for planned maintenance. The work was paused and the air supply was subsequently restored. No injury is reported in this evaluation case.

The initial notification does not establish whether the interruption began at the air source, within the distribution system, or at the receiving equipment. Supporting records will be provided as the investigation develops.

# Change and work-record requirements

Record ID: IA-D03 | Revision: 4 | Effective: 2024-03-01

Synthetic evaluation record. Fictional administrative requirements, not the partner's actual policy or a safe-work procedure.

## Change records

Section 3.2: When a service-routing change affects an existing maintenance boundary, the change owner identifies the affected energy-control procedure (ECP), drawing and receiving operating area. Engineering disposition is required before the changed arrangement is used for that maintenance boundary.

Section 3.4: Mechanical completion verifies the installed work covered by the completion sheet. Work-document disposition and distribution are separate signoffs. A drawing redline is not, by itself, an issued operating document.

Section 3.6: The affected ECP is either revised and issued, or an approved temporary instruction is attached to the work package. Draft preparation alone does not satisfy distribution.

## Work records

Section 5.1: The work package records the ECP revision supplied to the crew and the maintenance boundary's acceptance state. An initial notification may be entered before the event sequence has been checked.

Section 5.3: Competence and authorization records define the tasks for which a person is qualified. They do not record what that person actually observed or did on a particular job.

verificationFindings.issue: Evidence shows work in 'preparation' with acceptance pending but does not confirm whether specific components were verified as safe or complete; absence of a verification record is unknown status, not proof of failure.
verificationFindings.evidenceNeeded: Mechanical completion checklist, field sign-off, or inspection log confirming that installed work was verified before the event.
verificationFindings.question: Was there a signed mechanical completion check-list for 1SC dryer group D-101 prior to starting maintenance?

verificationFindings.issue: Work package references DW-1SC-17 but does not confirm the revision used or if it matched actual valve states; directory explicitly lacks real-time status data.
verificationFindings.evidenceNeeded: Copy of the configuration drawing (DW-1SC-17) actually used in the field and evidence that its revision was current at 09:31/10:00 AM.
verificationFindings.question: Which revision of DW-1SC-17 did the crew use, and how does it compare to actual valve positions observed?

verificationFindings.issue: The node asserts a 'Requirement for documented confirmation of understanding' as supported based on evidence noting the *absence* of interviews or logs. This is an error in logic: absence of records does not establish that a requirement existed; it only establishes what was recorded (or not). The claim conflates missing documentation with the existence of a formal barrier.
verificationFindings.evidenceNeeded: A procedure manual, work order instruction, or safety standard explicitly stating 'Documented confirmation of understanding regarding response steps is required before proceeding' for this specific task type. Without such text, the requirement cannot be established as existing in practice.
verificationFindings.question: Is there a written procedure (ECP, SOP, or Work Order Instruction) that mandates documenting a discussion on root cause assessment or response step confirmation prior to resuming work after an air interruption?

verificationFindings.issue: The node labels the status as 'unknown' but details it with language ('raises a hypothesis') that treats speculation about missing documentation as if it were evidence of a potential change. The contract forbids upgrading hypotheses into facts or treating blank fields as proof of absence without positive identification.
verificationFindings.evidenceNeeded: A revision history log for the ECP-1SC-04 document (Revision 3) showing changes between March and May, OR an explicit statement in the work package cover that a routing change occurred. Currently, only 'blank attachment field' exists, which is insufficient to confirm or deny a service-routing change.
verificationFindings.question: Does the revision history for ECP-1SC-04 show any modifications affecting RHOB boundary definitions between 2024-03-01 and May 20? If not, does the blank attachment field indicate that no such documentation was issued?

verificationFindings.issue: The node claims 'local indication P-R normally shows normal pressure band' as supported. The source text (IA-D01) defines the service area and mentions indicator P-R but does not define what constitutes a 'normal reading', nor does it establish that H-R was showing normal pressure at 9:31 AM or immediately prior to 10:00 AM.
verificationFindings.evidenceNeeded: A log entry, operator report, or system alarm record from RHOB operations confirming the status of indicator P-R (or header H-R) in the minutes preceding the incident. The directory alone cannot establish real-time condition data.
verificationFindings.question: What was the recorded value or state of local indication P-R at 09:45 AM and immediately before the pressure loss?

verificationFindings.issue: The node label asserts an event occurred ('Air-low indication appeared'), but the supporting source (IA-S01) explicitly states that 'Times and entries are reconstructed for the exercise' and does not identify the point at which air was interrupted. The evidence supports a log entry exists, not necessarily that the physical event happened exactly as described without further corroboration of system state. The node asserts an 'Air-low indication' event at RHOB P-R based on the shift log entry stating 'About 10:00 | RHOB | Air-low indication.' However, the source text explicitly states that times are reconstructed and entries do not identify specific points of interruption or provide captured numeric measurements. The claim relies solely on a desk entry which is admitted as potentially incomplete ('The desk entries do not log every field operation'). Without corroborating evidence (e.g., alarm logs, pressure readings) confirming the indication occurred at P-R specifically rather than generally in the area, and given the source's admission of reconstruction limitations, full support cannot be granted.
verificationFindings.evidenceNeeded: A record or measurement confirming the specific time and nature (source vs distribution) of the pressure loss to validate it as an actual incident rather than just a reconstructed narrative point. Corroborating record such as an instrument log or alarm history showing a specific 'air-low' signal triggered for header H-R/P-R around 10:00 AM to confirm the event occurred at that specific location and time rather than being a general observation.
verificationFindings.question: Does any other source confirm that the air-low indication at 10:00 AM was a physical event caused by supply interruption, not merely a log entry in a synthetic exercise?

verificationFindings.issue: The claim states the record 'was blank' at issue time. The evidence (IA-S02) explicitly lists WO-527-E as 'Blank at folder issue'. However, this does not prove it remained blank during execution or that no data was entered later; absence of filled content in a field is an observation, not proof of procedural failure unless the requirement to fill it before work began is established and breached. The claim conflates record state with action status.
verificationFindings.evidenceNeeded: Evidence establishing whether WO-527-E required completion prior to boundary preparation or if blankness at issue time constitutes a breach under Section 5.1 of IA-D03.
verificationFindings.question: Does the work package cover (IA-S02) requirement for 'WO-527-E' field execution record imply it must be completed before maintenance release, and is there evidence that U-A/U-B failed to complete it?

verificationFindings.issue: The claim infers no engineering disposition or temporary instruction was attached based on a blank attachment field. However, the absence of an entry in one administrative field does not prove that no change occurred elsewhere (e.g., verbal directive, separate memo). The evidence shows 'Temporary instruction attachment field: blank' but does not establish whether any service-routing change existed at all.
verificationFindings.evidenceNeeded: Engineering logs or change records for instrument-air routing between 2024-03-01 and May 20, 2024 to confirm if a change occurred that required disposition.
verificationFindings.question: Are there engineering logs showing any service-routing changes affecting RHOB instrument air during the period March–May 2024?

verificationFindings.issue: The node label asserts that the origin is 'currently unknown'. While this accurately reflects the current state of evidence in the packet (no SCADA trends provided), treating an absence of data as a confirmed condition ('unknown') without identifying what specific record would resolve it violates the instruction to separate facts from interpretations. The claim should be framed as a gap requiring resolution rather than a verified fact.
verificationFindings.evidenceNeeded: SCADA trend logs or field reports for the air header between 09:48 and 10:07 AM, specifically showing pressure drop location (source vs distribution).
verificationFindings.question: Do SCADA trends exist that show whether the pressure loss originated at the compressor source, within a specific branch valve, or downstream of the Utilities gallery?

verificationFindings.issue: The node label asserts 'Whether any field valves were open/closed... is unknown'. The evidence packet explicitly states in IA-D01 that it does not establish valve positions. Asserting this as a verified condition ('unknown') without citing the specific limitation of the document or requesting the missing execution record (WO-527-E) conflates 'missing data' with 'verified fact'.
verificationFindings.evidenceNeeded: Content of Work Order 527 Execution Record (WO-527-E), specifically valve status logs, P&ID snapshot at time of incident, or crew testimony regarding valve positions.
verificationFindings.question: Does the execution record for WO-527 contain a timestamped log or signature confirming which valves were open/closed during boundary preparation?

verificationFindings.issue: The node label asserts 'Communication breakdown... may have contributed'. The evidence shows RHOB requested attendance at 10:07 and Utilities paused work. There is no requirement or standard defined in the packet for response time to an air-low alarm during maintenance prep. Labeling this as a condition without establishing a breached prerequisite (applicable procedure) violates the instruction that 'A pending acceptance... does not establish unauthorized downstream work' nor procedural breach.
verificationFindings.evidenceNeeded: Standard Operating Procedure or Maintenance Plan defining required response times for instrument-air alarms when boundary preparation is in progress, and evidence of whether such a standard existed on May 20, 2024.
verificationFindings.question: Is there an applicable procedure that defines the maximum allowable time to respond to an air-low indication during maintenance boundary preparation?

verificationFindings.issue: The node asserts a 'potential unrecorded service-routing change' as an established condition creating a hazard scenario. The evidence only supports the existence of a blank attachment field (a documentation gap) and explicitly states that no record confirms whether such a change occurred or if recent changes were received by the crew.
verificationFindings.evidenceNeeded: Engineering logs, SCADA trend analysis for instrument-air pressure history between March 2024 and May 2024 to identify any routing modifications; witness testimony from U-A/U-B regarding receipt of change briefings.
verificationFindings.question: Did a service-routing change occur in the RHOB or 1SC dryer system between March 20, 2024 (policy effective date) and May 20, 2024?

verificationFindings.issue: The edge claims the blank field 'indicates a potential gap' that could have allowed a hazard to manifest. This conflates an administrative record state (blank form) with a physical causal mechanism without evidence of what changed physically or if any change existed at all.
verificationFindings.evidenceNeeded: Confirmation of whether a service-routing change actually occurred and the specific valve states involved; verification of whether the blank field represented a missing barrier to knowledge rather than just an empty administrative slot.
verificationFindings.question: If no routing change had occurred, would the air loss still have happened? If yes, this edge is invalid as it assumes causality from documentation gaps alone.

verificationFindings.issue: The node 'Origin of pressure loss' is labeled unknown in sources but the edge treats it as a direct cause. The incident description explicitly states origin is not established; treating an unverified condition (unknown) as a confirmed causal factor violates evidence boundaries.
verificationFindings.evidenceNeeded: SCADA trend logs comparing P-R (RHOB) with upstream nodes and other downstream points to determine if the loss originated at the source, distribution system, or local equipment.
verificationFindings.question: Do SCADA trends show pressure drops originating upstream of RHOB before 10:00 AM on May 20?

verificationFindings.issue: The edge claims an outdated drawing caused improper boundary preparation. Evidence shows no confirmation that crew U-A/U-B saw a different version or recent changes (claim-15w4fb1 is unsupported). The causal link relies on the unproven premise that they used an incorrect document.
verificationFindings.evidenceNeeded: Revision history of DW-1SC-17 and witness testimony confirming which drawing was held/used by crew U-A/U-B at 09:48.
verificationFindings.question: Did crew members hold or reference a specific revision number for DW-1SC-17 during the gallery work?

verificationFindings.issue: The edge claims communication breakdown caused delayed response. Evidence shows RHOB requested attendance at 10:02 and Utilities paused work; no evidence defines 'breakdown' or acceptable timing standards for this specific service.
verificationFindings.evidenceNeeded: Call logs between control rooms to verify message content, timestamps of acknowledgment vs action initiation, and definition of expected response time for air-low alarms during maintenance prep.
verificationFindings.question: What was the exact wording of RHOB's request at 10:02, and what specific actions did Utilities take immediately after receiving it?

verificationFindings.issue: The edge claims an unrecorded service-routing change created a hazard. Evidence does not establish that such a change occurred; the blank attachment field only indicates lack of documentation for temporary instructions, not necessarily a routing change.
verificationFindings.evidenceNeeded: Engineering disposition logs or maintenance records showing whether any instrument-air system modifications were pending on May 20 prior to WO-527 issuance.
verificationFindings.question: Were there any approved but unimplemented changes to the instrument-air distribution network in the RHOB area during Turn 2 of May 20?

verificationFindings.issue: The edge claims an unknown origin (external factors) caused the pressure loss without evidence of third-party logs or upstream outage records. The rationale speculates on external causes but lacks supporting source excerpts.
verificationFindings.evidenceNeeded: Utility logs, third-party notifications, or incident reports confirming an event at 10:00 AM from outside the facility.
verificationFindings.question: Do any utility distribution logs or third-party work orders exist for May 20, 2024 that show a pressure loss starting around 10:00 AM?

verificationFindings.issue: The edge attributes the cause to physical damage or blockage in the #1 slab caster system without inspection reports, fracture analysis, or leak detection logs. The cited source 'q-1g3wd0d' is not present in the evidence packet.
verificationFindings.evidenceNeeded: Inspection reports, fracture analysis results, or maintenance records for D-101 showing component integrity at 10:00 AM on May 20, 2024.
verificationFindings.question: Are there any field inspection logs or pressure test records from the morning of May 20 that document valve positions or equipment condition before the interruption?

verificationFindings.issue: The edge links a lack of evidence about drawing versions to the hazard scenario without confirming whether recent changes existed. The claim references 'claim-2x4nrr' which is not in the packet; no revision history for DW-1SC-17 or P&IDs is provided.
verificationFindings.evidenceNeeded: Revision control records, change orders, and dated copies of equipment-location sheets (DW-1SC-17) to verify if a recent configuration change was uncommunicated.
verificationFindings.question: Does the revision history for DW-1SC-17 show any changes between March 2024 and May 20, 2024 that were not distributed to the crew?

verificationFindings.issue: The edge claims an 'unknown' status for engineering disposition as a cause. The rationale relies on the *possibility* of missing records ('Change management records...'), not evidence that such records were absent or violated.
verificationFindings.evidenceNeeded: Evidence confirming whether Engineering Disposition was required by ECP-1SC-04 and if it existed/is available for this specific change, OR explicit confirmation that no disposition record exists in the system of record.
verificationFindings.question: Does a Change Management log exist for instrument-air routing changes affecting RHOB between Q1-Q2 2024? If yes, does it show an open or closed status for any relevant work orders?

verificationFindings.issue: The edge claims 'unknown' mechanical completion verification as a cause. The rationale assumes the absence of a form implies non-compliance without establishing that such a form was required at this specific work stage ('preparation') or if an alternative verification method existed.
verificationFindings.evidenceNeeded: Evidence defining whether Mechanical Completion Verification is mandatory for *all* preparation activities under IA-D03, and evidence of any completed checklists (even informal ones) used by the crew before 10:00 AM.
verificationFindings.question: Under current procedure IA-D03, is a formal 'Mechanical Completion' form required specifically during the 'preparation only' stage described in WO-527? If not, what alternative verification was performed?

verificationFindings.issue: The edge claims 'unknown' drawing currency as a cause. The rationale assumes outdated drawings are the only risk without evidence that the crew *actually used* an incorrect version or failed to notice discrepancies.
verificationFindings.evidenceNeeded: Copied configuration drawing from the crew's folder (as listed in source q-1qywya4) OR field inspection logs showing which specific P&ID/drawing revision was referenced during the 09:31 briefing and used for valve identification.
verificationFindings.question: Please provide a copy of the specific instrument-air configuration drawing or P&ID that Crew U-A/U-B carried to site on May 20, 2024. Does its revision date match DW-1SC-17 (Rev A)?

verificationFindings.issue: The edge claims a causal relationship between 'unknown status of documented confirmation' and delayed response/pressure loss. The evidence packet explicitly states the initial notification does not establish where interruption began (source: incident-description). There is no evidence that communication breakdown caused pressure loss; only that it *may* have contributed to misunderstanding, which is speculative.
verificationFindings.evidenceNeeded: Call log between control rooms showing timing of air-low alarm acknowledgment and response actions relative to pressure restoration.
verificationFindings.question: Did the Utilities team acknowledge receipt of the air-low alarm before or after pressure was restored? If yes, how long did it take?

verificationFindings.issue: Similar to edge-glhywu: this node asserts an unknown communication breakdown as a potential cause. However, no evidence supports that such a breakdown occurred or caused delay; the packet lacks call logs/radio recordings (sourceIds include q-isvv2m which is empty). The competing explanation notes upstream issues may be responsible.
verificationFindings.evidenceNeeded: Radio recordings of 10:00 AM exchange between RHOB and Utilities desks/field crews to verify if communication breakdown occurred or delayed response.
verificationFindings.question: Were there any recorded communications indicating confusion, delay in acknowledging the alarm, or misinterpretation during the event?

verificationFindings.issue: This edge suggests incomplete shift log entries may have contributed to pressure loss. However, missing field data (valve states) does not prove causality; it only indicates lack of detail. The counterfactual assumes misconfiguration caused the issue without evidence.
verificationFindings.evidenceNeeded: Field execution record WO-527-E if available, or equivalent documentation showing valve positions and actions taken during boundary preparation.
verificationFindings.question: What were the actual valve states at 09:48 AM? Were any valves inadvertently left open/closed contrary to procedure?

verificationFindings.issue: The node 'No documented confirmation of understanding' is not supported by evidence; shift logs record events but do not confirm lack of crew understanding. The causal link to pressure loss relies on an unsupported condition.
verificationFindings.evidenceNeeded: Interviews or records showing whether the crew understood root cause/response steps, and proof that such documentation was required at this stage.
verificationFindings.question: Did any log entry, briefing record, or interview indicate a gap in shared understanding of the air-low event's origin or response?

verificationFindings.issue: The condition 'Maintenance acceptance signature was not yet signed' is supported as a fact (finding-fakvn3), but asserting it caused pressure loss requires evidence that incomplete boundary preparation could cause upstream air failure. The competing explanation of upstream issues remains unrefuted.
verificationFindings.evidenceNeeded: Evidence linking the unsigned status to an inability to isolate or verify valve states, and proof that such a state contributed causally rather than coincidentally.
verificationFindings.question: Was there any procedure requiring mechanical completion verification before boundary release? If so, was it performed?

verificationFindings.issue: The barrier 'Requirement for engineering disposition' is a documented requirement (IA-D03 Section 3.2), but there is no evidence that a service-routing change occurred or that Engineering disposition was bypassed. The claim assumes an unrecorded hazard without positive proof.
verificationFindings.evidenceNeeded: Change management logs, routing diagrams, and engineering approval records for Q1-Q2 2024 to confirm whether any changes affected the instrument-air boundary.
verificationFindings.question: Were there any service-routing changes affecting the RHOB instrument-air system between March 2024 and May 2024?

verificationFindings.issue: The node 'node-elx3yo' (Potential service-routing change) is labeled as a hypothesis ('raises a hypothesis') and explicitly marked with status 'unknown'. The edge asserts this unknown condition caused the event. Evidence does not confirm an unrecorded routing change occurred; it only confirms documentation gaps.
verificationFindings.evidenceNeeded: Physical inspection reports, SCADA trends showing pressure loss origin (upstream vs downstream), or maintenance records confirming a specific valve state change between 2024-03-01 and May 20.
verificationFindings.question: Did the air interruption originate from an unrecorded service-routing change at node-elx3yo?

verificationFindings.issue: The rationale claims a 'communication breakdown' contributed to the event. The evidence (shift log) shows a request for attendance and subsequent pause but does not define this as a 'breakdown' or establish that clear communication would have prevented the air loss.
verificationFindings.evidenceNeeded: Call logs, alarm acknowledgment timestamps, and defined response-time requirements for RHOB/Utilities coordination to determine if delays were abnormal.
verificationFindings.question: Was there an established procedural requirement violated by the delay between 10:00 (alarm) and 10:02 (pause), or was this a normal operational pause?

verificationFindings.issue: The node 'node-xyzr01' is labeled as having an unknown origin. The edge asserts the event was caused by this condition (unknown origin). This violates causal discipline: a cause must be established before asserting it triggered the effect.
verificationFindings.evidenceNeeded: SCADA trend logs for P-R vs other points and maintenance records of leaks to confirm if the loss originated upstream, downstream, or within distribution.
verificationFindings.question: Where did the pressure loss originate (source header H-R, distribution system leak, or receiving equipment)?

verificationFindings.issue: The edge claims 'caused' by n-1wi4o7r (air-low indication) to the focal event. The evidence does not establish that a specific prior condition or action caused this particular interruption; it only records the occurrence of an air-low state and subsequent restoration.
verificationFindings.evidenceNeeded: Evidence establishing the physical cause of the pressure loss at 10:00 AM (source, distribution system failure, valve position change) is missing. The current evidence only confirms the event occurred but not its root mechanism.
verificationFindings.question: What specific equipment or process condition caused the air-low indication to appear at RHOB P-R at approximately 10:00 AM?

verificationFindings.issue: The edge claims 'contradicted-by' that the boundary was not released. While evidence confirms no signature existed (node-pu71er), this condition does not logically contradict or explain a pressure loss event; it merely describes an administrative state at the time of occurrence.
verificationFindings.evidenceNeeded: Evidence linking the lack of release to any procedural gap contributing to the failure is missing, as none exists in current records. The edge misrepresents the relationship between administrative status and physical cause.
verificationFindings.question: Does the absence of a maintenance acceptance signature indicate that an isolation step was omitted or that equipment remained energized when it should have been isolated?

verificationFindings.issue: The edge claims 'contradicted-by' due to the directory's limitation. However, this is not a contradiction but an explicit document scope statement (it does not establish valve positions). The evidence supports that we cannot infer physical states from IA-D01; it does not contradict any causal claim about pressure loss.
verificationFindings.evidenceNeeded: A current piping diagram or field observation record to confirm actual valve states at 10:00 AM is needed if the investigation intends to evaluate isolation completeness.
verificationFindings.question: Is there a current piping diagram, P&ID revision, or field log that records valve positions for the RHOB service station and dryer aisle as of May 20, 2024?

verificationFindings.issue: The edge claims a causal link from 'Origin of pressure loss (unknown)' to the event without establishing that an origin exists or identifying it. The rationale admits uncertainty ('upstream, distribution, or equipment') and cites no evidence for any specific failure mode.
verificationFindings.evidenceNeeded: SCADA trends showing where pressure dropped first; maintenance logs confirming leaks between 08:10 (normal) and 10:02 (low); physical inspection records of the air source/distribution line at that time.
verificationFindings.question: What SCADA data or field observation confirms whether the interruption originated upstream in the distribution system versus downstream equipment failure?

verificationFindings.issue: The edge hypothesizes an 'unrecorded service-routing change' as a cause but provides no evidence that such a change occurred. The blank attachment field does not prove a routing change happened; it only shows lack of documentation for whatever was attached.
verificationFindings.evidenceNeeded: Change management records (IA-D03) showing whether any instrument-air system modifications were initiated or completed between 2024-03-01 and May 20, 2024; engineering disposition documents if changes existed.
verificationFindings.question: Were there any service-routing changes to the RHOB instrument-air system in Q1-Q2 2024 that required ECP revision or temporary instruction attachment?

verificationFindings.issue: The edge asserts a barrier failure ('engineering disposition not met') without confirming whether a service-routing change actually occurred. If no change existed, the requirement (IA-D03 Section 3.2) may not apply.
verificationFindings.evidenceNeeded: Confirmation of any recent routing changes affecting RHOB; evidence that engineering disposition was sought or waived for those specific changes.
verificationFindings.question: Did a service-routing change occur in this case? If yes, is there an approved temporary instruction or revised ECP attached to WO-527?

verificationFindings.issue: The claim relies on a missing field execution record (WO-527-E) to assert that mechanical completion verification was not met. The evidence only shows the form is blank at issue time; it does not establish whether physical verification occurred before or during preparation.
verificationFindings.evidenceNeeded: Field inspection logs, valve status records, or witness testimony confirming whether isolation and mechanical completion were verified prior to 10:00 AM.
verificationFindings.question: Did the crew perform a field check of valve states and confirm isolation integrity before proceeding with work at approximately 10:00 AM?

verificationFindings.issue: The claim assumes a requirement for documented confirmation of understanding regarding response steps exists but lacks evidence that such documentation was mandated or required in this scenario.
verificationFindings.evidenceNeeded: Procedure documents specifying whether written confirmation is mandatory for air-low events during preparation phases; call logs showing discussion content between Utilities and RHOB at 10:02 AM.
verificationFindings.question: Is there a procedure requiring documented acknowledgment of response steps when an instrument-air low indication occurs during maintenance preparation?

verificationFindings.issue: The claim infers that the crew may have used an outdated drawing without evidence they actually did so. The blank temporary instruction field does not prove use of a different version.
verificationFindings.evidenceNeeded: Copies or logs showing which configuration drawings were physically present at the work site and referenced by U-A/U-B during preparation; briefing notes indicating specific versions discussed.
verificationFindings.question: Which revision number of DW-1SC-17 was carried to the field, and did either crew member reference a different version than Revision A?

verificationFindings.issue: The edge claims a 'communication breakdown' caused or contributed to delay based on an inference node that is itself unsupported ('unsupported', 'unknown'). The evidence packet contains no call logs, message timestamps, or procedural definitions of acceptable response times. Asserting causality requires establishing both the existence of a specific communication failure and its impact relative to normal procedure.
verificationFindings.evidenceNeeded: Call logs between RHOB and Utilities for 09:58–10:07 showing content/acknowledgment; definition of standard response time for 'air-low' alarms in this context.
verificationFindings.question: What specific messages were exchanged between the control rooms at 10:02 versus 10:07, and does the procedure define a maximum allowable interval before field attendance is required?

verificationFindings.issue: The edge treats 'no documented confirmation' as a condition that limits causal inference. However, the absence of documentation does not prove non-compliance or lack of understanding; it only proves an evidence gap. The node is labeled 'partially-supported', but using this uncertainty to assert a limiting condition on causality without establishing what was actually understood violates the instruction: 'Absence of evidence is not evidence that something did not occur.'
verificationFindings.evidenceNeeded: Interview transcripts or call logs confirming whether crew understanding occurred orally; definition of required documentation for such confirmations.
verificationFindings.question: Did the Utilities supervisor verbally confirm with Crew U-A/U-B at 10:02–10:07 that they understood the pause and next steps, even if not logged?

rejectedEdges.fromLabel: Loss of instrument air pressure in RHOB area during maintenance preparation
rejectedEdges.toLabel: Work package cover indicated blank temporary instruction attachment field.
reasons: The model pointed from the focal event toward a pre-event causal condition.

proposal.rationale: The blank temporary instruction field (condition n-1ps9rte) does not prove a service-routing change occurred, but it creates an information gap that prevents verification of whether the crew was aware of changes. This uncertainty contributes to the inability to confirm if standard barriers were in place.
proposal.counterfactual: If a service-routing change had occurred and been documented, the blank field would be an anomaly; if no change occurred, the blank field is normal. The event (air loss) happened regardless of which state was true.
proposal.competingExplanation: The air pressure loss originated from upstream or distribution system issues unrelated to local boundary preparation documentation.
proposal.evidenceGap: Whether a service-routing change actually existed between 2024-03-01 and May 20, 2024.

proposal.competingExplanation: The air pressure loss was caused by an upstream event that bypassed local boundary conditions entirely.

# Record and measurement conventions

Record ID: IA-D02 | Revision: 1 | Effective: 2024-04-01

Synthetic evaluation record. Conventions apply to this fictional case only.

## Measurements

Pressure values are bar gauge. A pressure tag names the measurement point, not every location on the service. The point register is needed to interpret location and scope. A running indication is not a flow measurement. A command, a field-position observation and a proved internal valve condition are different records.

## Time and identity

Wall times are local plant time on the stated date. Handwritten records are approximate unless stated otherwise. An alarm's occurrence time, acknowledgment time and export time may differ. Record aliases can persist after equipment changes; the title displayed on an alarm is not a substitute for its input mapping.

## Status conventions

# Instrument-air interruption during maintenance preparation

Record ID: IA-I01

Synthetic evaluation record derived from a historical incident. Not an actual company record or operating instruction.

At approximately 10:00 AM on May 20, 2024, during Turn 2, the RHOB process area reported loss of instrument-air pressure while a two-person Utilities team was preparing the #1 slab caster (1SC) compressor/dryer system for planned maintenance. The work was paused and the air supply was subsequently restored. No injury is reported in this evaluation case.

The initial notification does not establish whether the interruption began at the air source, within the distribution system, or at the receiving equipment. Supporting records will be provided as the investigation develops.
